sections.content: The whole course is wrapped around VBA (duh). James uses his dedicated website rather than the canvas module. This makes it very confusing to follow and do self-study. The VBA content is also not that useful and practical. For the majority, you are NOT going to use VBA.
sections.teaching: James seems like a nice guy, equipped with some degree of enthusiasm. However, this still doesn't make up for the lack-luster content organizing. It's quite hard to not get distracted after 5-10 minutes. His English is pretty good and can understand easily.
sections.grading: Have not yet released the grade. Check other review for this section.
sections.workload:
This workload is light. No attendance. Only 1 group assignment and 1 individual assignment. The Main one is final exam which consist of 70%. In the assignments, James explicitly mentioned AI is allow to use.

Tho, take note that the course material is not easy to self-study. There are plenty of files in one category, and there is sub category, and there is 4+ files. You basically don't have what to learn and what to skip. Again, this has made this course very hard to juggle with. There is only minimal pages of PPT (5 page average), and there are no annotation regarding the flow.

sections.content:
In terms of content, what he teaches is actually pretty useful. However, it is very poorly presented because he has a website with four ways of presenting the same info, and then has Canvas. It's hard to know which one to even look at and follow.

Thus, I think this deserves a D grade, which I rarely would give.
sections.teaching:
Whilst the way he teaches content in terms of organisation is undoubtedly poor, his teaching is not too bad but not good.

For example, he does explain the business perspective of VBA such as why some specific object should be a string and not a long/double eg.

He does forget to explain some key concepts such as why need option explicit.
sections.grading: Not graded yet will update but I believe it won't be good
sections.workload: Workload is not big because its just final, assignment and then hw, which for 3 credits is pretty good imo. However, it's a lot of workload to self-study and figure out hwat he taught adn what he didnt teach. Thus, I think to save yourself the workload it is much better to just attend the lesson and save yourself the hassle.

sections.content: No idea why there is a three credit course on a programming language that microsoft does not even bother updating the IDE for.  It is like a basic programming course for any language, including variable declaration, loops, arrays, subroutines and worksheet/cell/range manipulation. And the syntax of it is like pseudocode in igcse computer science and it is very annoying. To be fair, vba can be very useful in certian scenarios but it is suppose to be a lightweight time saving tool for spreadsheet calculation not for making a whole program with UI and all that
sections.teaching: His teaching is not good. I skipped half of the lectures. You don't need to attend his lectures to learn vba. The lectures are just him going through programming questions in a slow pace while constantly stressing about how everyone should follow his long list of coding requirements otherwise he will deduct points. Just attend the lab sessions to learn.
sections.grading: There is 10% on a in class group exercise which is very easy as long as you know how to use vba. 20% is on an assignment where you have to create a complicated program, and this part can take some time. 70% is on the final so it basically determines your fate. The final  is not very easy, not very difficult. You have to get a near perfect score to be in A range. I got 87% overall and got B+.
sections.workload: Before the assignment there really is barely any workload. The assignment will take some time to complete. In the final they provide cheatsheet so you don't have to memorize most of the code.

sections.content:
Just see the attached syllabus.
Ofc the McDonald's Ordering for teaching.
An assignment about FIFO. It seems they change the content a bit every semester cuz my friend used buttons for the assignment last sem, but we used a UserForm this semester. The content is also different for the group exercise.
sections.teaching:
From what my friends and the TA told me, James cares a lot about 'user-friendliness.' So it's pretty common to lose marks on small but 'careless' mistakes like button placement, unclear naming, or missing message box titles, especially when you're in a hurry or nervous during the exam.

Also requires lots of self-learning like finishing the lab exercises cuz what he covers in class only gives you a basic understanding of the topic. You’ll likely forget it soon after the lecture if you don’t reinforce it on your own.
sections.grading:
Guess the grading system did show some improvements after he changed the syllabus so I’m here to provide a more updated/fairer comment.

Homework (20%): 94/100 (Mean: 79.8, UQ: 92.81)
Group Exercise (5%): 4.5/5 (Mean: 3.8, UQ: 4.63)
Final Exam (75%): 55/75 (Mean: 43.4, Median: around 44.75, UQ: around 61, cuz it got 3 separated scores for the final and I just sum up each of their medians/UQs which is slightly deviated from the total median/UQ)

Most of my marks are slightly lower than the UQ and I got a B+ so the grading makes sense given 25% A range.
sections.workload:
Decent. There’s just one assignment (which took me three days to complete) and one in-class group exercise. You only need to watch the lecture video related to the exercise topic. Both allow the use of ChatGPT.

The final exam covers some lab concepts but very few, if any, lecture topics (from my experience). Since there are no lab recordings, you now know what not to miss. He also provides a cheatsheet, though it’s not very useful. By exam time, you’ll already remember basic code snippets (like how to reference the last row). Plus, you won’t have time to search the cheatsheet for what you need.

Memorizing every line of code isn’t wise, but knowing the universal workflow for each question type is key. For example, with array questions, remember to declare the array, count the size, redim the array, and fill the array with data.

The course materials are quite useful in real-life when working, can simply adapt the VBA flow into other work-life usage.

sections.content:
Some basic VBA stuff, u could refer to other reviews for detailed syllabus which I'm too lazy to post here XD

VBA itself isn't a very commonly used programming language, but I agree that it does no harm to just learn about its basics. However, I give the content C for its stupid arrangements.

For one thing, the instructions of in-class exercises are never clear and there are always tons of questions in the chat room every time an exercise was released.

If that isn't enough, there are a lot more things even worse. For example, it made us hard code 10 message boxes in in-class exercise 1 and not allowing us to use loop as it wasn't taught; the instruction of assignment 1 was that we should ask the user to import file using path name, but if u really do so, ur mark get deducted cuz they say importing by path name is troublesome and u should design something more "user-friendly" ????
sections.teaching:
The professor and TA could articulate clearly and they explain the concepts fairly well. A major problem however, is that the lecture slides DO NOT cover all the syntax that we need to know.

Every lecture, the professor would come up with some cases randomly and demonstrate how to write all those codes, which often involve syntax not covered in the slides, and so it takes extra time to make notes on that.

Moreover, they stress "business application" which in other words are just making useless designs or trivial changes. NO U DONT WANT TO STRESS BUSINESS APPLICATION, U SHOULD STRESS PROGRAMMING LOGIC AND HOW ALGORITHMS ARE BUILT.

sections.content:
Basic VBA teaching

ONE REMINDER: MAKE SURE YOUR CLASS DO NOT CONTAIN QFIN PEOPLE

Each year in fall semester, there are 38-40 qfin year 2 pre-registered into this course. Make sure not only your class, and also other section with same professor do not contain QFIN people. Otherwise you will face crazy grading curve.

Note for qfin students: there is two ways to avoid facing the crazy grading curve
1. register in year 1 Spring semester, since you are not required to take ISOM 2010 before this course (only first batch qfin can do this)
2. swap away in year 2 fall (but I can tell you it is extremely difficult, although I am using this way)  Remember, swap away means to swap from one prof to another, but not different section of same prof
sections.teaching:
I think the professor try his best in explaining the concept with concrete example and hand on experience. But, I cannot find the value of the lesson. Most likely I leave after 30-40 minutes. If there is no in-class quiz, I think I will not appear.

The TA Bosco is very good TA. He is able to deliver the requirement of the homework in a clear and concise way. He is also able to figure out the focus of each professor. And, most importantly, ask him everything about assignment. He, but not professor, mark the assignment. Make sure you satisfy his requirement. He marks quite in detail. sections.workload:
Two assignment, one mid term and one final exam.

One assignment is to use Visual Basic to write a simple program. (The content varies in different semester, but still not that difficult. This is an individual assignment, but TA will help a lot if your willing to ask.)
Another is to use VBA to write a macro in Excel. (In my semester is to write a macro that downloads the data automatically from the web and plot a graph in Excel. This is a group assignment, so it is not that difficult.)

Mid term was mainly focusing on VB. As I remember, no cheat sheet was allowed. Same, it was not that hard.

Final was mainly focusing on VBA, they would provide you a cheat sheet that showed all the basic concept (which was almost the same as the revision notes that they distributed before the final exam). So the course overall is quite easy.

sections.content:
A blended learning course, meaning you will need to watch video lectures. In 1 week, 1 class will be used to watch the video on your own (no need to come to class) and the other class will be used for reviewing the video lectures and doing in-class exercises (group). After watching the video lecture, you will need to answer questions in the online quiz (3 attempts).

You will form a group in which you will work with throughout the course (for the in-class exercises and the group assignment). The in-class exercise will be given and submitted from Google Classroom. Some of the questions will be similar to those in exam.

Lab is somewhat useful to practice your programming skills. Do come to the lab sessions as there will be 2 lab demonstrations throughout the course. You will then need to show the TA how your program works.

Course materials:
1. Visual Basic
- Data
- Input/Output
- Conditional Statements
- Looping
- Arrays
- Methods
=== MIDTERM ===
2. VBA:
- Class and Objects
- Excel Objects (Workbooks and Worksheets)
- Range Objects (Cells Manipulation)
3. Business Applications:
- Data Manipulation and Validation
- Implementing Formula
=== FINAL (non-cumulative) ===

Every class before the exam, the professor will go through the types of exam questions as a guideline to study.

Overall, the content is very appropriate for students with no programming background.
sections.teaching: The professor makes sure everyone understands the materials and is willing to answer your questions. In class, he sometimes ask question to random students. Even though it is okay to not get the right answer, try to listen to what he is saying and be prepared for his questions. On the class before each exam, he gives guidelines, which I think is very useful as it clearly states what will be tested in the exam.
sections.grading:
Grading:
Midterm Exam: 20%
Final Exam: 30%
Lab Assessment (4% each): 8%
Assignment (15% each): 30%
Online Quiz (1% each) And Discussion (1% overall): 12%

The midterm was quite tricky, so pay attention to the details as some programs may lead to errors. The final was relatively easier, made up of MCQ, short answers, and long answers (write a program). Cheat sheet is given, even before the exam day.
sections.workload:
Lab assessment is pretty easy as long as you can make the program by yourself. The questions asked in the lab demonstration will be basic, only to test your understanding towards the flow of your program.

Assignment 1 (individual) is to write a program (calculation game) in Visual Basic (VB). Just follow the guidelines and you will be fine.

Assignment 2 (group) is to write a program (stock analyzer) in VBA. It is harder than assignment 1 but you can work with your group to figure it out.

Online quiz will be given every week to make sure that you watch the lecture video. Point will be given if you can get all answers correctly within 3 attempts. Make sure to finish your quiz before the deadline (5 pm of the day before the next class).

Discussion can be done anytime and you will only need to post in canvas or send an e-mail once to get the point. You can either ask a question or answer the questions in canvas.

sections.content:
A course about very basic VB and VBA programming language.

This course is designed to train students to understand programming, in particular business applications programming. Students will learn why we need to use programming in their professions and why they build business applications, how business applications influence business workflows, how programming could be more beneficial and useful in business applications, and so on. Students will learn basic programming syntax and structure, and how to build basic business applications using high-level programming languages.
